title: Per-change eval snapshots + intelligent alert routing for model/config updates
creator: Maya Patel
description: Overview: Ship a Console-driven workflow that captures an immutable eval snapshot for every model or config change, automatically computes delta metrics vs. a chosen baseline, and routes high-confidence regressions to the right on-call or owner with deduplicated, context-rich alerts (Slack + PagerDuty). Goals: 1) surface only actionable regressions to reduce noise; 2) provide connective context tying a regression to the exact model version, config diff, and recent rollout policy; 3) enable engineers/PMs to triage from Console with links to PRs, artifact diffs, and runbooks. Scope: - Backend: snapshot store for eval artifacts, diff/aggregation service, routing rules API. - Console: new Eval Change view showing side-by-side metric diffs, top failing tasks, and linked artifacts. - Alerting: Slack messages with collapse keys; PagerDuty integration using dedupe keys and routing by owner tag. Non-goals: full signal-ML auto-remediation and automated rollbacks in this phase.
acceptance_criteria: 1) When a model or config is promoted, the system records an immutable eval snapshot (metrics + example failures + config metadata) and indexes it with change metadata (commit/PR, deploy id, user). 2) Console shows a per-change delta card with at least three diff visualizations (aggregate metric delta, per-task failure rate, representative failing examples) within 3 clicks from the model page. 3) A configurable alert policy triggers when regression confidence > threshold and SLO drop > configured delta; alerts published to Slack channel and PagerDuty service with a dedupe key that groups related regressions from the same change. 4) Deduping works: repeat triggers for the same change consolidate into a single thread/message rather than generating noise. 5) Owner-based routing sends PagerDuty incidents to on-call team tagged in model metadata and posts an owner-mention in Slack. 6) Console UI includes a ‘Mark false positive’ action that records feedback and suppresses further alerts for the same signature for 7 days. 7) Basic audit trail exists for snapshots and alert deliveries (success/failure logs).
notes: Design review 2025-02-12: move forward with immutable snapshot store instead of mutable rollup to simplify rollback/tracing.
Trade-offs: snapshot retention vs. storage cost — initial policy = 90 days default, configurable per org; potential follow-up to tier snapshots by cardinality.
Decision: use dedupe key composed of (model-id, change-hash, alert-signature) to balance sensitivity vs. false merges.
Follow-up: explore ML-driven alert prioritization in next cycle (low effort baseline now, plugin later).
